title: Computational reliability and numerical audits
scope: Read-only audit of the complete manuscript and eight solutions, delayed answers, synthetic input, program, README and independent checker. Reviewed source records for scope alignment without repeating external source retrieval. Only this peer-review record was written; no manuscript, program, shared state, publishing or child-agent operation was performed.

findings.location: content/chapters/v04-c11.html, Assertions, validation and tests serve different purposes
findings.text: A JSON number can be a boolean or float after decoding
findings.issue: JSON booleans are a distinct JSON type. The intended warning is valid for a purported monetary field whose decoded Python value has the wrong type, but the current sentence incorrectly calls the boolean a JSON number.
findings.suggested_change: A purported monetary field can decode to a boolean or float; silently converting it to integer cents can lose information.
findings.impact: Editorial precision only. The actual exact-type validator correctly rejects booleans, floats and strings and remains active under -O. No numerical result or gate depends on this wording.
findings.status: resolved: root applied the suggested wording; peer verified the corrected sentence in the manuscript

review_conclusions.conditioning_and_stability: Correctly separates sensitivity of the exact target from algorithm error and states the perturbation model. The componentwise relative sum condition number is derived by the triangle inequality, including attainability of its bound, and output-relative conditioning is left undefined at an exact zero net. Absolute error remains meaningful. Backward stability is described with its error model and supported problem scope; cancellation is not incorrectly equated with unstable subtraction. A backward-stable sum can have poor relative forward accuracy on an ill-conditioned sum.
review_conclusions.sum_bound: The product expansion and geometric majorant justify gamma_k = ku/(1-ku) for k = n-1 and ku < 1. Represented inputs, normal-range round-to-nearest operations, no overflow and no problematic underflow are explicit assumptions. The first input is used directly, so n-1 additions is appropriate. The implementation computes the bound with exact Fraction arithmetic on the represented binary values and separates net conversion error from subsequent accumulation. Original integer sums stay exact even when their values exceed binary64's exact-integer range.
review_conclusions.variance_identity_and_sensitivity: Independently expanded the unordered pair identity, yielding population variance equal to pair-square sum divided by n squared. The centered implementation subtracts the integer anchor before float conversion. The input perturbation expansion is correct; the cross term is bounded by 2 eta sqrt(V), and the error variance is at most eta squared. Squaring a nonnegative rearrangement permits independent exact-rational verification of the inequality without relying on floating square roots. Zero variance and common translation are treated correctly. The engineering comparison budget is explicitly distinguished from a global numerical theorem and economic measurement error.
review_conclusions.units_and_targets: Population-list variance uses n; the n-1 calculation is correctly tied to the usual iid wider-population unbiased estimator. Cents-to-USD variance conversion divides by 10000, not 100. Sum-error budgets have cents units; variance sensitivity and error budgets have cents-squared units. Standard error is not confused with either variance target. A matching scalar sum does not establish nonmutation, completeness or truthful measurement.
review_conclusions.exercises_and_retention: Solved and matched every determinate part of all eight exercises, reviewed the explicit criteria for the contract and reproduction memo, and checked the added delayed answers. All values agree. The constant-zero and wrong-denominator examples show why transformations alone cannot certify a variance routine. The explicit validation replacement rejects booleans and survives optimization. Both retention results, exact net3 versus sequential float4 and variance8/3 cents-squared =1/3750 USD-squared, are correct.
review_conclusions.implementation_and_inference_scope: Strict file schema, duplicate-field handling, nonfinite rejection, supported bounds, exact reference arithmetic, audit-gate behavior and recorded hashes match the documentation. Fixed broken-variant fixtures remain separate from user-modified data. The five boundary cases inspected preserve the supported runtime assumptions. The program's pass status is appropriately limited to listed computations/fixtures, and finite tests are not represented as economic validation or a proof for every modified program. No substantive defect was found.

limitations: This is an independent computational and written specialist audit, not external human academic certification or proof of all possible executions.
Finite perturbation and boundary checks complement, but do not replace, the reviewed algebraic proofs and stated binary64 assumptions.

recommendation: Ready for root acceptance. The low-severity JSON-type wording correction is verified as resolved; no material mathematical, arithmetic, solution or executable-gate finding remains.
